incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July approving the consolidated Capital Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital – LSC), particularly Articles 4, 19-22, 58-64, 62 and 102; supplemented by Royal Decree 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil – RRM) on registration mechanics.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) for the negative name certificate; provincial Registro Mercantil (Commercial Registry) of the province of the registered office for the mandatory company inscription; Ministry of Justice as supervisory body.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (public incorporation deed) granted before a Spanish notary and mandatorily inscribed in the Registro Mercantil within the statutory timeline (LSC Articles 19-21).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital for an SL: EUR 3,000 (LSC Article 4.2), fully subscribed and fully paid in cash at the moment of execution of the deed (LSC Article 62); the deposit must be evidenced by a bank certificate, and no escrow account is required because the entire capital is paid up at incorporation. Non-cash contributions must be valued in the deed. Legal reserve of 10% of annual profits until reaching 20% of share capital is mandatory (LSC Article 274). Note: the originating payload flag 'minimum_capital_requirement: false' is factually incorrect for an SL and is overridden by the imperative provisions of the LSC.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: UNANIMOUS WRITTEN RESOLUTIONS of the Founding Shareholder of [Company Name], S.L., adopted at the incorporation meeting. First: the draft Escritura de Constitución is approved, and the share capital of EUR 3,000 is subscribed and fully paid in cash as required by Articles 4 and 62 LSC. Second: the registered office is fixed at [street, city], Spain, and the full corporate purpose covering video-game anti-cheat middleware and software integrity is confirmed. Third: [Full Name, ID] is appointed Sole Managing Director (Administrador Único) and irrevocably accepts office. Fourth: the Managing Director is authorized to file the deed in the Registro Mercantil, apply for the company NIF, open bank accounts, pay form 600, and complete all registrations required to commence operations. Passed unanimously on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance Certificate (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry), Ministry of Justice – online filing portal; CIRCE platform optional for expedited SL creation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application requesting at least three proposed corporate names in descending order of preference. The Central Registry verifies that no identical or confusingly similar company name exists and issues a negative name certificate valid for three months. The certificate must be delivered to the notary at execution of the deed.
required_dossiers: Official name-certificate application form
Up to three proposed SL corporate names
ID copies of the founding shareholders
Payment receipt of the name-certificate fee (approx. EUR 30)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is rejected as identical, confusingly similar or misleading, the Registry issues a certificate of rejection; refile immediately with additional alternative names. No penalty is incurred and the fee is not forfeited.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and Provisional Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any Spanish credit institution; the bank issues the statutory capital-deposit certificate (certificado de desembolso).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate account in the name of the company in formation and pay in the full share capital of EUR 3,000 in cash. Obtain a bank certificate evidencing the deposit, which must be attached to the incorporation deed. Funds must not be withdrawn until the deed is executed and filed.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association (bylaws)
Copy of the negative name certificate
Passport or NIE of all signatories and beneficial owners
Proof of address of the future registered office
Initial capital deposit of EUR 3,000
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the transaction under AML/CFT rules, provide source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declarations; a corrected release of the deposit certificate is issued within one to two business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Granting of the Public Incorporation Deed before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A Spanish notary (Notario) of the province where the registered office will be located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Approve the final bylaws in the deed: corporate name, share capital of EUR 3,000, registered office, corporate purpose (development, sale and maintenance of video-game anti-cheat engine and software integrity middleware), share distribution, administration structure and legal-reserve rule. All shareholders must appear in person or by legal representative. The notary verifies capacity and legality, receives the capital-deposit certificate and the name certificate, authorizes the deed and issues certified copies for registry filing.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate with confirmed validity
Bank certificate of capital deposit
Passports or NIEs of shareholders
Proposed bylaws in Spanish
Notarial fee payment (tariffed by Royal Decree 1426/1989)
Prior communication of form 600 for stamp-duty payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary objects to a clause (e.g., non-compliant corporate purpose, capital rule or directors' powers), amend and restate the articles by a supplementary declaration before execution; the expected delay is one to three business days with no government penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – provincial delegation or online via form 036.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after the deed is granted, file form 036 (declaración censal) with the AEAT to obtain the provisional NIF/CIF of the company in formation. Commercial operations may begin only after the definitive NIF is issued upon successful inscription in the Registro Mercantil.
required_dossiers: Certified copy (copia autorizada) of the incorporation deed
First copy of the deed stamped by the regional tax office for AJD payment
Completed form 036
Notary's deed communication where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NIF application is rejected for missing stamping of the deed, pay the corresponding AJD tax through form 600 at the regional treasury and resubmit form 036 within ten business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration in the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver to the provincial Registry an authenticated copy of the deed, evidence of payment of the Transfer Tax and Stamp Duty (AJD – Actos Jurídicos Documentados) and, where applicable, the notary's certificate under Article 114 RRM. The Registrar legally reviews the deed, issues the inscription and gives public validity to the company. Obtain the registration extract (certificación de inscripción) for the definitive NIF application.
required_dossiers: First authorized copy of the incorporation deed
Proof of payment of AJD via form 600
Notary certificate of appointment of administrators (Article 114 RRM)
Registry application form
Payment of the official registry tariff
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Suspensions or rejections (calificación negativa) are cured by a supplementary deed correcting the defect or by filing an appeal (recurso gubernativo) with the Mercantile Registry directorate within two months; in practice, a notarial rectification takes five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Security Enrollment and Municipal Operating License Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS) and the local Ayuntamiento (City Council) of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, obtain the company's employer registration code (código de cuenta de cotización) with the TGSS and enroll the corporate officers and administrative staff in the appropriate social-security scheme (RETA for administrators, general scheme for employees). Concurrently, submit the activity-commencement declaration to the city council and request the municipal operating license (licencia de apertura) for the office premises; office-based software design generally fits the municipal catalogue of compatible professional uses.
required_dossiers: Company registration certificate from the Registro Mercantil
Definitive NIF/CIF certificate
Form TA.6 / TA.7 for employer registration
Lease contract or ownership title of the registered office
Municipal technical memorandum (memoria técnica) and building-license fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal license is rejected or subject to third-party objections, submit a compliance-response letter (respuesta al requerimiento) with the required technical corrections; digital professional activities enjoy favorable municipal classification, and re-submission takes approximately ten business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no industrial license is required for ISIC 6201 (software development) under Law 21/1992 (Ley de Industria); the only establishment-level authorization is the municipal Licencia de Apertura obtained from the local Ayuntamiento.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Apertura / Declaración Responsable de Actividad Económica (municipal establishment license for office premises).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITECO) for national coordination; competent regional environmental authority of the corresponding Comunidad Autónoma for project approvals.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category V: the office-based anti-cheat software activity is not listed in Annexes I, II or III of Law 21/2013 on environmental assessment; no full EIA report and no activity-specific environmental registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – no point-source industrial discharges or VOC emissions. Residual obligations: office wastewater and urban solid waste are managed through municipal networks per Law 7/2022 on waste; electronic equipment scrap must be handed to an authorized waste manager; low-voltage electrical equipment poses no air-emission threshold.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-prevention conformity certificate (certificado de protección contra incendios) per Technical Code CTE-DB-SI and, where applicable, Royal Decree 2267/2004 for server-room electrical installations; low-voltage electrical installation certificate (boletín eléctrico) per Royal Decree 842/2002; occupational risk-prevention assessment under Law 31/1995 covering computer workstations, fire exits and first-aid equipment; structural load report not required for standard office occupancy, but the landlord must confirm suitability of the leased premises for the declared professional use.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – Sede Electrónica: sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es; corporate registry: Registro Mercantil Central (www.rmc.es); AEAT Central Office: Calle Infanta Mercedes 37, 28020 Madrid.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Obtain the provisional NIF (NIF provisional) from AEAT via Form 036 before notarization. Step 2: Execute the public deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución) before a Spanish notary and register the SL in the Mercantile Registry. Step 3: File Form 036 (declaración censal) with AEAT within one month of incorporation; AEAT issues the definitive NIF (9-character code; legal form letter such as B for SL, followed by seven digits and a control character, e.g., B12345678). Step 4: Simultaneously register for IVA (VAT), IRPF withholding, and employer social-security obligations in the same census filing. Non-resident shareholders require no Spanish TIN; non-established foreign suppliers claiming VAT refunds under the 13th Directive must file Form 361 and appoint a Spanish tax representative for refund purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) is an autonomous corporate taxpayer subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Ley 27/2014, LIS) at the 25% general rate (15% for the first two taxable periods of newly created qualifying entities; 4% under the Zona Especial Canaria regime). Spanish tax residence follows incorporation or effective place of management (art. 8 LIS); resident SLs are taxed on worldwide income. No pass-through treatment applies; dividends and capital gains qualify for the participation exemption (art. 21 LIS) subject to minimum holding and substance conditions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain has no US-style check-the-box election. Available statutory elections: (1) reduced 15% CIT rate for newly created entities (art. 29.1 LIS); (2) consolidated tax group regime (arts. 58-64 LIS) – binding 3-year election requiring at least 75% common control; (3) ETVE holding-company regime with prior AEAT notification and substance requirements; (4) Patent Box (art. 23 LIS) – 60% exclusion of qualifying IP income from patents and software on a nexus basis; (5) R&D&I tax credits (art. 35 LIS) with optional binding advance valuation agreements; (6) VAT OSS/IOSS schemes for cross-border B2C supplies (returns filed on Modelo 369); (7) monthly VAT refund regime (REDEME, art. 30 RD 1624/1992) available by election to exporters; (8) SII real-time reporting regime – mandatory for taxpayers over EUR 6 million turnover, elective below that threshold. ATAD hybrid-mismatch rules (arts. 15 ter-15 nonies LIS) are mandatory and not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA) – value added tax under Ley 37/1992 (LIVA), RD 1624/1992, implementing Council Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No domestic de minimis threshold: every Spanish-established business must register for IVA from the first taxable supply via Form 036. Intra-EU distance sales of goods and electronically supplied services to consumers trigger Spanish VAT only above the EUR 10,000 pan-EU distance-selling threshold (art. 73 LIVA); non-EU suppliers of electronic services are taxable from the first transaction and must register through the OSS or obtain a direct Spanish NIF-VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información): businesses with turnover above EUR 6,000,000 and all REDEME monthly-refund taxpayers must transmit issued and received invoice records (libros registro) to AEAT via authenticated web services (XSD schemas, digital certificate or Cl@ve PIN) at sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es within four calendar days (maximum eight) of issuance or receipt. Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece), implemented by RD 1007/2023, mandates structured electronic invoicing (Facturae or equivalent interoperable formats) for B2B transactions, phased in one year after the final Ministerial Order for taxpayers with turnover above EUR 8 million and two years for all remaining taxpayers. The planned 'Verifactura' system will extend near-real-time invoice clearance and QR-code stamping to all taxpayers; today no universal cryptographic invoice stamp exists, but invoices to the public sector require the Facturae 3.2 format with AEAT COD certification.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to non-EU destinations are exempt with credit (0% VAT) under art. 21 LIVA provided physical departure from EU customs territory occurs within 90 days of delivery. Intra-Community supplies are exempt under art. 25 LIVA where the customer has a valid EU VAT ID, supported by Modelo 349 recapitulative statements and transport evidence. B2B supplies of services to non-establishment customers, including SaaS, software licensing, and kernel-level anti-cheat middleware integrity services, fall outside Spanish VAT under the place-of-supply rule (art. 69.1.1º LIVA) when the customer is established abroad and identified by a valid non-Spanish VAT number. B2C remote e-supplies to non-EU individuals are also outside Spanish VAT (art. 70.1.3º LIVA). Loss of documentary substantiation converts the supply into a taxable transaction at 21%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DUA – Documento Único Administrativo (Single Administrative Document) export declaration accepted and authorized by Spanish Customs (SIGA/SISTEMA), including the exit confirmation
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note evidencing physical departure of the goods within the 90-day statutory window

Commercial invoice (factura comercial) with Incoterms, exporter NIF, item description, and HS classification (e.g., 8471/8523/4907 for physical media; service contracts for digitally delivered licenses)
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 evidencing collection of export proceeds from the foreign buyer
Packing list, certificate of origin where required, and T1 transit document when the goods exit via another EU member state
For intra-EU supplies: customer VAT ID validated via VIES, Modelo 349 recapitulative statement, and transport contracts evidencing delivery terms
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT Export Verification Plan and Customs Audit Area conduct targeted audits of zero-rating claims; the burden of proving physical exit rests entirely on the exporter (art. 21.1 LIVA). Where export is not completed within 90 days of delivery, the exemption is clawed back and VAT is assessed at 21% on the full invoice value plus late-payment interest (interés de demora, art. 26 LGT) and executive-collection surcharges (arts. 27-28 LGT). Misdeclaration triggers penalties of 50%-150% of the amount (art. 191 LGT); obtaining undue refunds is penalized under art. 193 LGT; fraud exceeding EUR 120,000 per corporate year constitutes a criminal tax offence (art. 305 Código Penal) punishable by 1-5 years imprisonment and fines up to six times the defrauded amount. The clawback window is four years (art. 66 LGT), extended to ten years where amounts are held in tax haven jurisdictions (art. 66 bis LGT). The 180-day standard FX repatriation deadline governs internal compliance and balance-of-payments reporting; Spanish VAT law itself imposes the 90-day dispatch rule rather than a fixed currency repatriation deadline, although exchange-control obligations (Banco de España statistical declarations, Modelo B1) apply to commercial settlements with non-residents.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (BdE) is the national monetary and financial-supervision authority operating within the European System of Central Banks (ESCB) and the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM). Foreign-exchange declarative control and foreign-investment screening coordination sit with the Dirección General de Transacciones Exteriores of the Ministerio de Economía, Comercio y Empresa, while anti-money-laundering supervision over credit institutions is jointly exercised by SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain applies full euro convertibility under the EU Treaty framework (TFEU Articles 63-66) for both capital-account and current-account operations; there is no exchange-control licensing, no prior authorization for ordinary profit remittance or dividend distribution, and no requirement to convert foreign currency revenue into EUR. Residual restrictions exist only for transactions targeted by EU/UN sanctions, cash-carrying limits, and mandatory fiscal and AML declaration duties. An ES_SL (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada) may remit dividends, loan repayments, royalties and services income to non-resident shareholders or counterparties without BdE approval after discharging corporate income tax (25% under Impuesto sobre Sociedades), non-resident withholding tax (19% general rate, reduced by bilateral tax treaties), and the applicable balance-of-payments statistical filings. Full convertibility is nevertheless conditioned on the correct ex-post or ex-ante filing of foreign investment declarations and banking supporting documentation; failure to file may trigger administrative fines but does not create a convertibility barrier.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no mandatory surrender, forced conversion or repatriation timeline for export proceeds; the euro is freely convertible and EU rules prohibit currency controls on current transactions. However, the ES_SL must observe the statistical declaration regime of Banco de España and the Agencia Tributaria: export operations and related collections exceeding established thresholds must be declared monthly within the statutory filing windows for balance-of-payments statistics (operaciones de comercio exterior), invoices must be VAT-compliant for continuous intra-Community supplies, and the Intrastat/VIES obligations apply when applicable. Treasury best practice is to channel export receivables through a licensed Spanish or EU bank account (or passporting EMI) so that auditability, VAT refund eligibility, and Banco de España reporting are preserved; retention of proceeds in foreign bank accounts is lawful but increases compliance burden and may raise transfer-pricing scrutiny.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Multicurrency EMEA) / Capital Contribution Receiving Account
Operational Account with SEPA and SWIFT Business Access

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: HIGH for payment-acceptance and low-value disbursement rails; MEDIUM as a sole primary operating-account anchor. EU-licensed electronic-money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions passporting into Spain under PSD2 (e.g., Wise Europe S.A., Currencycloud, Airwallex, and other e-money institutions registered with the BdE or a home EU regulator) may provide IBAN accounts, multi-currency wallets and faster cross-border wires without obtaining a Spanish banking license. However, they generally do not act as collecting banks for the statutory Declaración de Inversiones Exteriores, cannot issue certificates of account residence acceptable to the Agencia Tributaria, and offer limited or no documentary credit (LC), cheque clearing, and formal FX statistical reporting services. The optimal treasury architecture is a hybrid model: a tier-1 Spanish bank holds escrow/operational capital and trade-clearing accounts, while a reputable passporting EMI is used for low-value subscriptions, developer payouts, and cross-border disbursements to LATAM and Asia corridors.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under Ley 10/2010, as amended by Royal Decree-Law 7/2021, remote corporate onboarding is legally possible using qualified digital identity verification, e-signature, and a compliance interview conducted by secure audio-video means. In practice, Banco de España-licensed tier-1 banks mandate at least one physical or high-assurance videoconference entrevista personal (face-to-face interview) with the compliance officer, conducted at a Spanish branch or through a recognized notary; the directors or an appointed mandatario with a valid power of attorney (poder notarial) must attend. For a fully non-resident-owned ES_SL, banks commonly require: (i) a Spanish tax representative, (ii) evidence of registered office and real activity (lease contract, licencia de apertura, or substantive service contracts), and (iii) original or apostilled constitutional documents, with the CIF/NIF, UBO register extract, and powers of attorney translated by a certified sworn translator. Physical appearance at a Spanish branch materially accelerates onboarding; a purely remote flow is viable only with fintech EMIs or select banks with specialized non-resident onboarding desks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBOs generating high-value cross-border wires within the first 60 days of opening, with no local substance evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original/apostilled certificate of incorporation and statutes of the ES_SL; extract from the Registro Mercantil and Beneficiarios Reales registry identifying all UBOs; notarized powers of attorney and passport copies of signatories; audited or bank-reference-confirmed source-of-funds documents (shareholder bank statements, tax returns, sale agreements); board resolution approving treasury policy and account signatories; Spanish NIF-VAT registration certificate; and a cash-flow forecast consistent with the anti-cheat SaaS business plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Classifier flags ISIC 6201 as adjacent to gambling/gaming risk due to the 'gaming' keyword in commercial name.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ES_SL bylaws excluding gambling and betting activities; DGOJ (Dirección General de Ordenación del Juego) compatibility statement or confirmation that anti-cheat integrity middleware does not require gambling authorization; product technical documentation (kernel-level anti-cheat engine, EULA, privacy and security certifications); target-customer contracts with software publishers; and a tax classification certificate showing software-development, not gambling, ISIC codes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Round-trip payments between the Spanish entity and related entities outside the EU without clear commercial rationale.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Arm's-length transfer pricing documentation prepared in accordance with OECD Chapters I-V and Spanish transfer-pricing statutory rules (Royal Decree 634/2015); executed intercompany services and IP licensing agreements; monthly or quarterly platform usage and invoice logs of the anti-cheat engine; board minutes and pricing benchmarks for similarly situated middleware vendors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital contributions requiring purpose-code matching where declared capital exceeds statutory minimum (€3,000 for SL).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: D-1 or D-2 form (Declaración de Inversiones Exteriores) plus photocopy submitted to the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores or filed with the notary; deed of capital increase (escritura de aumento de capital) or certified shareholder loan contract for capital advances; bank transfer instructions citing SWIFT purpose code GSCR or corresponding local code 'Aportación de Capital'; UBO declaration; proof of source of funds for amounts over €3,000; and, where applicable, the pre-investment screening clearance under EU FDI screening mechanisms.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for the ES_SL: non-resident shareholders remit EUR via SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA CT for EU-origin funds) to the tier-1 Spanish operational account, referencing the statutory foreign-investment declaration (D-1/D-2) and the internal bank purpose code corresponding to 'Capital Contribution / Share Capital Increase' or 'Préstamo de Socios' (shareholder loan). For equity, the notarial escritura or a private deed filed with the Registro Mercantil and investment registry must evidence the contribution; for loans, a certified facility letter and the D-2 form must be filed with the Secretaría de Estado de Comercio within the statutory window. The bank's AML desk will require UBO certificates, source-of-funds documentation, and board resolutions before crediting escrow-class funds. For intra-group inbound wires covering software royalties, services or license fees, the funds must be tagged with the correct Banco de España statistical balance-of-payments code and backed by commercial invoices to avoid reclassification as capital injections requiring formalities.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for export-oriented disbursements of the anti-cheat middleware business: (1) SWIFT MT103 for high-value and non-EUR supplier payments (USD, GBP, JPY), with explicit purpose codes and supporting invoices retained for BdE statistical reporting; (2) SEPA SCT and SEPA Instant per SCT B2B for intra-EU vendor, payroll and SaaS infrastructure disbursements; (3) commercial documentary credits (letter of credit) under UCP 600 and standby LC/URDG 758 for procurement of hardware server equipment and strategic licenses from Asia/LATAM counterparties; (4) international factoring and forfaiting of receivables via CESCE-backed export credit insurance for key gaming-platform customers; and (5) bank-guaranteed payment undertakings. All outbound service payments are subject to corporate deductibility checks, export e-invoicing, and withholding tax on Spanish-source payments to non-resident licensors under treaty provisions, requiring the collection of tax residence certificates.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD and EUR/GBP OTC deliverable FX forwards executed under ISDA/IFEMA documentation
FX swaps (FXS) and cross-currency swaps (CCS) to hedge long-dated commercial receivables or intercompany loan exposures
Plain-vanilla FX vanilla options on freely convertible EUR pairs as permitted under MiFID II
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for third-currency country exposures where the bank does not provide deliverable settlement in emerging-market currencies (e.g., ARS, BRL proxy hedges)
Currency-swap structures in EUR and other fully convertible currencies for balance-sheet hedging, subject to bank ISDA and credit documentation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales): balance sheet, profit-and-loss account, statement of changes in equity, and notes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) through the electronic filing service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders must approve annual accounts within six months after the fiscal year-end; deposit must occur within one month after approval. For a calendar-year SL, approval by 30 June and deposit by 30 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-deposit penalty under Ley 14/2013 ranges from EUR 1,200 to EUR 12,000 per instance; the SL loses access to certain registry certifications; persistent non-deposit may lead to closure of the registry sheet and eventual dissolution or administrative strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades), Modelo 200
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the tax year-end; for calendar-year SLs, the filing window is 1–25 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Voluntary late filing surcharges of 5%, 10%, or 15%, plus late-payment interest; formal penalties up to EUR 6,000 or 15% of the tax amount; understatements may trigger additional penalties of 50%–75%. Tax debts may lead to embargo procedures but do not directly trigger administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual legalization of statutory corporate and accounting books (legalización telemática de libros)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) telematic legalization service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year SL, books must be legalized by 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-legalized books lose evidentiary value and are inadmissible as accounting proof; the registry may reject subsequent filings; directors face liability for accounting deficiencies; monetary sanctions can be imposed under Article 39 of the Commercial Code. Continued default is treated as a good-standing failure but is not an immediate strike-off trigger.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual informative declaration of transactions with third parties, Modelo 415
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year SL, due 1–28 February following the year in which total transactions with any third party exceed EUR 3,000.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties under the General Tax Act range from EUR 150 to EUR 6,000 depending on the volume and nature of omitted operations; no direct strike-off effect.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies to an SL that exceeds at least two of the following three indicators for two consecutive financial years: total assets greater than EUR 2,850,000; annual net turnover greater than EUR 5,700,000; average number of employees greater than 50. Audit is also required when the SL belongs to a group that is consolidating or when required by sectoral legislation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish generally accepted accounting principles (Plan General de Contabilidad, PGC 2007) as approved by Royal Decree 1514/2007; SMEs may apply the PGC de PYMES; listed groups and financial institutions must apply IFRS-EU; Spanish GAAP is aligned with EU accounting directives.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Ley 10/2010 and Ley 6/2023, the SL must maintain accurate internal ultimate beneficial owner (t titular real) information and file changes into the Single Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners within ten business days of any relevant shareholding transfer. Spain does not require a separate calendar-year UBO renewal filing; however, before each annual accounts deposit the SL must internally confirm that the Register of Members and the UBO register are consistent with all shareholding movements made during the year.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays: 15% reduced rate for newly created entities during the first two years of taxable profit (minimum taxable base EUR 3,000 for prior-year profitable entities); 30% tax credit for R&D activities and 20% for innovation-related investments under Spanish R&D&I incentive regime; Patent Box 60% exemption on qualifying IP income; regional scale-up tax incentives may apply under Basque Country/Foral regimes but are not applicable to standard national SL.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed electronically through Agencia Tributaria (AEAT) electronic office; mandatory for all resident companies; payment/direct debit or refund request through the same portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following six months after the tax period end (for calendar year-end: 25 July each year). Non-calendar tax periods: by the 25th day of the month following the six-month anniversary.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification data: NIF (tax identification number), legal name, legal form code, registered tax address, and corporate domicile.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide Spanish NIF; non-resident entities must appoint a Spanish fiscal representative for service of process; foreign tax IDs not accepted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net profit (resultado contable) before corporate tax adjustments, per Spanish General Accounting Plan (PGC) financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile from PGC-compliant local GAAP; maintain reconciliation schedules; foreign GAAP basis not directly accepted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income attributable to a permanent establishment (PE) for non-resident entities or branch attribution of profits under DTA Article 7.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholder without PE does not file Modelo 200; PE income is taxed at 25% under Non-Resident Income Tax Law; claim DTA PE rules through Modelo 210/216 if treaty applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax credits (retenciones e ingresos a cuenta) on Spanish-source income including dividends, interest, and royalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident recipient must file Modelo 210 or Modelo 216 to obtain refund of excess withholding; attach TRC and identify DTA beneficial ownership clause.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of prior-year tax losses (base imponible negativa compensable) against current taxable base; maximum 70% of taxable base for entities with turnover > EUR 20 million, 60% for turnover between EUR 1–20 million.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Spanish PE losses may be offset only under Article 19(2) Non-Resident Income Tax Law; same 5-year and cap rules apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity classification determining applicable CIT rate: standard 25%, reduced 15% for new SMEs, 30% for credit institutions/hydrocarbon entities, 0%/1% for qualifying funds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reduced new-SME rate only for Spanish-resident entities; PE taxed at 25%. Non-resident holding company status does not qualify for SME rates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of related-party transactions and transfer pricing documentation obligations under Article 18 LIS; references Form 232 details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all intragroup transactions with Spanish SPV; prepare Local File/Master File/Country-by-Country report as applicable; failure to include Form 232 triggers separate penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge of 5% of tax due plus 1% per month up to 20 months (max 20%). After 20 months: 20% plus arrears interest (currently 5%). Late filing without tax due: fixed penalty EUR 200–EUR 6,000. Failure to file Modelo 232 or TP documentation: EUR 1,500–EUR 20,000 per infraction. Loss of tax credits and 30% surcharge on late payments.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% on dividends/other income distributed by Spanish resident companies to non-resident shareholders. 0% for resident Spanish corporate shareholders applying participation exemption (Article 21 LIS). Reduced DTA rates may apply (often 5% or 10%).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident shareholder must: (1) obtain Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from residence state tax authority, apostilled/legalized if needed; (2) file Modelo 210 (Non-Resident Income Tax Return) or Modelo 216 (Annual Summary of non-resident withholdings) to claim refund of excess withholding; (3) submit TRC electronically via AEAT, together with beneficial ownership self-certification; (4) provide paying Spanish company with supporting documents before or within 30 days from payment. Without TRC, 19% withholding applies and refund claims must be submitted within four years. Anti-abuse (PPT/LOB) may deny treaty benefits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 19% for royalties and interest to non-residents. Treaty rates: generally 10% for royalties and 10% for interest under most Spanish DTAs (e.g., Spain-US, Spain-Singapore). EU Interest & Royalty Directive: 0% for associated EU companies with at least 25% direct/voting ownership, subject to LOB. Higher withholding (24%) applies to non-EU/non-treaty jurisdictions without information exchange procedures. Patent Box and royalty characterization require beneficial ownership and substantive IP.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if intragroup transaction volume exceeds EUR 1,000,000; Master File required if consolidated group revenue >= EUR 90,000,000; Country-by-Country Report threshold EUR 750,000,000 group revenue (EU DAC4); Form 232 mandatory for related-party transactions > EUR 250,000 aggregated.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not maintain a standalone ESR regime, but substance requirements under OECD BEPS Action 5, Article 15 LGT (substance over form), GAAR/PPT under MLI apply. Spanish shell entities lacking personnel, premises, decision-making, and real activity risk recharacterization, denial of treaty benefits, and 25%–50% surcharge penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting Spanish-source middleware license income; using Shell S.L. to channel anti-cheat licensing profits without substance; failure to file Modelo 200 for two or more consecutive years; manipulating invoices for software development to reduce taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 305 Criminal Code: imprisonment 1–5 years and 6x fine of defrauded tax (administrative 50%–150% of underpayment); criminal threshold EUR 120,000/year. Article 191 LGT surcharge 50%–150% of unpaid tax; mandatory business closure up to 6 months in aggravated cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors jointly liable under Article 42.2 LGT; civil restitution of unpaid taxes; asset freezes, travel bans, passport surrender; disqualification from managing companies up to 10 years; imprisonment 1–5 years for criminal tax fraud; personal confiscation of proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Shell Company & Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining Spanish S.L. with no real staff, premises, or operational activity solely to own IP or channel royalties to low-tax jurisdiction; artificially interposed entity without commercial rationale; hybrid mismatches reducing withholding by treaty shopping.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT recharacterizes transaction, denies DTA benefits, reassesses income at 25% tax plus late payment interest and penalties up to 50%; administrative fines EUR 1,000–EUR 15,000 per annual non-compliance period; judicial dissolution under Article 104 Companies Act; loss of tax credits and losses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for insolvency deficits under Article 367 Ley de Sociedades de Capital; travel bans and exit restrictions; dischargeable debts become non-dischargeable; fines under Art. 386 LGT up to EUR 10,000 for facilitating shell presence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the gaming anti-cheat Spanish entity as conduit for funds from undisclosed beneficial owners, undeclared foreign bank accounts, or phantom licensing contracts with no underlying service; failure to file Modelo 720 for offshore assets exceeding EUR 50,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal Code Article 301: imprisonment 6 months–6 years and fine up to 3x laundered value; Modelo 720 late/unfiled penalties: EUR 1,000 per item, 150% of hidden amount for undeclared values exceeding EUR 10,000; seizure of Swift/Stripe accounts; AML administrative sanction up to EUR 5 million or 10% of annual turnover.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors with knowledge are criminal accomplices/principals; travel bans and asset seizures; personal liability for fines and restitution; disqualification from corporate directorships; personal estate confiscation for willful AML facilitation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure & False Reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intragroup royalty/licensing payments to parent or IP company without valid TP study; absence of Local File/Master File/Form 232; profit mark-ups outside interquartile range; manipulating comparability adjustments to avoid Spanish taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT adjusts to arm's-length, imposes 25% CIT on adjustment, interest, penalties: 15% of adjusted amount if documentation partially conforming, 50% if documentation non-complete, up to EUR 20,000 additional for Form 232 omission; criminal tax offense if adjustment exceeds EUR 120,000/year.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for 40% of penalty under Article 375 LGT if willfully negligent; imprisonment, travel bans, confiscation of bank balances, prohibition on management; civil indemnity to corporate group for tax deficiency.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File Annual Accounts and Dissolution Irregularities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Abandoning Spanish S.L. without formal dissolution and liquidation; not filing annual accounts for two consecutive years; extracting liquidating dividends or capital as 'service fees' without liquidation or withholding; failure to file Modelo 200 for the winding-up period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Mercantile Registry closure of company sheet; Modelo 200 omission penalties up to EUR 6,000 even for zero returns; constructive dividend treatment of unauthorized distributions at 19% withholding plus Artt. 25 LGT surcharge; forced liquidation and cancellation of registration; AEAT estimated taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for all company debts including tax liabilities under Art. 42.1.c LGT; travel bans and embargoes; asset seizure; liability for missing annual accounts and dissolution formalities.
